title: A top-level literal scalar with an indentation indicator of 1 keeps the first space
notes: The bare document is `s-l+block-node(-1, block-in)` (production 207), so the literal scalar is parsed with n = -1, and its content indentation is n + m = -1 + 1 = 0 (productions 170 and 163). The line ` foo` has no indentation to strip, and its space is content: the value is a space, `foo`, and a line feed. The same arithmetic gives the yaml-test-suite results for entries of a block sequence at column 0 (4QFQ and R4YG: `|1` over `  explicit` reads ` explicit`) and for mapping values (M5C3, F6MC). A competing reading, the one libyaml uses, counts the indicator from column 0 at the top level too (content indentation 1) and reads `foo` followed by a line feed. That departs from the productions, which put the top-level node at n = -1, so the kit follows the productions. No yaml-test-suite case decides the top-level form.

provenance.reference: A reader that gave `foo` for this input, treating the indicator as an absolute column at the top level.
